references.text: Moses asks to know God's ways after God says He knows Moses by name and has found favor in his eyes.
Moses again asks for favor in God's eyes and requests that God go with them, referencing that Israel is His people.
David asks God to teach him His ways, reflecting Moses' prayer to know God's ways.
The psalmist asks the Lord to teach him His way, paralleling Moses' desire to know God's ways.
Refers directly to God making His ways known to Moses in response to Moses' prayer in this text.
Moses reminds God that the Israelites are His people and His inheritance, reflecting the argument in this prayer.
Moses appeals to God by calling Israel God's people, using the same reasoning as here.
Jesus defines eternal life as knowing God, connecting to Moses' desire to know God.
Prophetic fulfillment of Moses' prayer; God's promise to give a heart to 'know' Him directly answers Moses' request.
Thematic parallel: Both prayers are about leading the people to 'know' God and turn back to Him.
Contrastive parallel: The same phrasing ('favor in your eyes') is used in two opposing situations (a prayer for guidance versus a prayer for death).
Theological fulfillment: God's promise in Ezekiel answers Moses' prayer to preserve the relationship 'my people - your God'.
